subject: Hosted evaluation — next steps and rate/profile questions
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: Arman Shah <arman@carthop.com>, Lina Park <lina@carthop.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 05 Jul 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted evaluation — next steps and rate/profile questions

Hi Arman / Lina,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — great conversation. I promised to pull together a short follow-up with the items we discussed so your engineering and infra teams can evaluate the Hosted API path quickly. Below is a recap and a few targeted questions that will help us provision a sandbox that matches your traffic profile.

Recap (demo highlights):
- You liked the live chat latency and the streaming UX for agent responses.
- Two main features: chat for live support (contextual session state + tool calls) and embeddings for product search re-ranking.
- Primary constraint: US-only data residency and 30-day retention for customer data in the pilot.

Information we need from CartHop (so we can configure the sandbox and rate caps):
1) Preferred deployment for the pilot (hosted API, dedicated pool, or private VPC). From our call you leaned toward Hosted for speed of onboarding — can you confirm?
2) Traffic profile for the pilot:
   - Expected peak QPS (requests/sec) during support peak hours
   - Average tokens per request (in/out) for chat flows (rough ballpark is fine)
   - Concurrency for embeddings indexing jobs (if any) and expected batch size
3) Endpoints you want in the sandbox (examples: /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings, /v1/re-rank)
4) Any nonstandard security/compliance asks (SAML, SCIM, specific KMS provider)
5) Target timeline for the pilot (start date and duration)

Quickstart footsteps for Hosted evaluation (what we will provide once we get the above):
- Sandbox API key and scoped credentials (token lasts 30 days for the pilot).
- Two sandbox endpoints: a chat endpoint and an embeddings endpoint (we’ll provide hostnames in the next email).
- Default rate caps: we’ll start with a conservative slice (10 QPS chat, 5 QPS embeddings) and a documented burst policy. We can scale quickly after we see traffic.
- Prefix/KV caching enabled for session-heavy chat to reduce token usage — we’ll enable by default in the sandbox.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short checklist for the Hosted quickstart and a sample ratecaps CSV we can use to map your traffic to our endpoint quotas.

Proposed next steps:
- Reply with answers to the 5 questions above (2–3 bullets is fine).
- I’ll provision sandbox access within 48 business hours once we have your expected peak QPS and endpoint list.
- If you want a quick sync with engineering to review network egress, we can set a 30-min call next week.

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben on pricing and burst/SLA options depending on the profile you share.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments:
- redwood-hosted-quickstart-checklist.pdf (1 page)
- ratecaps-sample.csv (sample mapping file)

On Wed, Jul 5, 2028 at 3:12 PM Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Arman / Lina,
>
> Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — great conversation. I promised to pull together a short follow-up with the items we discussed so your engineering and infra teams can evaluate the Hosted API path quickly. Below is a recap and a few targeted questions that will help us provision a sandbox that matches your traffic profile.

Thanks Olga — this is great. Quick answers below (happy to expand):

1) Deployment preference for pilot
   - We want to start with Hosted API to iterate fast. If the pilot looks good, we may evaluate Dedicated in Q4.

2) Traffic profile (pilot estimates)
   - Peak QPS (chat): ~50 QPS (peak support windows, roughly 2 hours/day)
   - Average tokens per chat request: ~400 tokens in (user) / ~250 tokens out (assistant) — these are averages; some sessions will be longer.
   - Embeddings: episodic indexing jobs, concurrency ~4 workers, each sends batches of ~256 texts.

3) Endpoints
   - /v1/chat (priority)
   - /v1/embeddings (for nightly re-indexing and on-demand search)

4) Security/compliance
   - US-only data residency required for pilot
   - SAML for SSO but not needed immediately for the sandbox
   - We need clarity on data retention settings and audit logs (who can access logs)

5) Timeline
   - Pilot target start: 2028-07-12
   - Pilot duration: 6 weeks

Two quick asks from our side: can you provide an estimated unit-cost range for the hosted slice that covers ~50 QPS chat + embeddings indexing (ballpark USD/month)? Also interested in the burst policy (how long burst capacity can run) and SLA guarantees for latency.

Thanks — I’ll loop Lina to share any infra network constraints.

—
Arman Shah
Head of Product, CartHop
arman@carthop.com | +1 (212) 555-4421

Thanks Arman — this is super helpful. I’ve summarized below and attached the quickstart with next-step checkboxes so your infra team can hand off details.

Summary of CartHop pilot profile (per your note):
- Deployment: Hosted API (pilot) — consider Dedicated for Q4 if utilization grows.
- Peak chat: ~50 QPS (2-hour window).
- Tokens: ~400 tokens/user avg in, ~250 tokens out (session average).
- Embeddings: batch jobs, 4 concurrent workers, batch size ~256.
- Data residency: US-only; retention 30 days.

What we’ll do next (and timeline):
1) Sandbox provisioning: we’ll provision a Hosted sandbox slice scoped to your profile and enable US-region tenancy. ETA: by 2028-07-08 EOD once you confirm network allowlist.
2) Rate caps & burst: default sandbox caps will be 20 QPS chat, upgradable to 50 QPS after we see traffic; burst policy: short bursts to 2x baseline for up to 5 minutes (production policies differ; Ben will propose a production burst/SLA option).
3) Pricing signal: I’ve looped Ben (cc) — Ben, can you provide a ballpark hosted monthly cost range for 50 QPS chat + embeddings indexing? Include guidance on reserved vs on-demand economics.
4) Security: we’ll enable audit logging and surface retention controls in the console; SAML can be added during pilot but not required for access.

Next steps for CartHop:
- Reply with the IPs CIDR block for network allowlist (or confirm you want a token-only sandbox with no allowlist).
- Confirm you’re OK with the sandbox ETA above (2028-07-08).
- If you want a pricing call, Ben and I can do 20 minutes on Friday.

I’ve attached the quickstart checklist and the sample ratecaps CSV with a sample mapping based on your numbers.

Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0187
